message:
QUESTION:
Under company policy, which of the five stores should receive this year's refurbishment budget?

DATA:
Five-store retail chain, financial year 2025. A refurbishment budget is available for one store. Company policy: the budget goes to the store with the lowest annual sales per square foot of sales floor (the company's space-productivity KPI), measured on a full-year basis.

| Store | Annual sales 2025 | Sales floor area (sq ft) | Gross internal area incl. stockrooms (sq ft) |
| North | £2.4m | 8,000 | 10,000 |
| South | £3.6m | 15,000 | 18,000 |
| East | £1.8m | 6,000 | 9,000 |
| West | £2.1m | 10,000 | 12,000 |
| Central | £4.2m | 12,000 | 14,000 |

Annual sales 2024: North £2.3m, South £3.5m, East £1.7m, West £2.9m, Central £4.0m. Floor areas were the same in 2024.

Operations note: West was closed from January to March 2025 (3 months) for flood repairs, so its 2025 sales cover 9 trading months. All other stores traded for all 12 months in both years. The flood repairs were covered by insurance and did not change the store's layout.

KNOWN FLAWS:
F1. [method] The company KPI is sales per square foot of sales floor, not gross internal area. Using gross area changes the densities and their relative gaps. CORRECTION: Sales-floor densities (2025 as reported): North £300, South £240, East £300, West £210, Central £350.
F2. [calculation] £4.2m / 14,000 = £300, not £320 (even on the draft's gross-area basis). CORRECTION: £300 per sq ft gross (or £350 on sales floor). Central is 50%, not 'roughly 60%', above South and East on gross area.
F3. [omission] Ignores that West traded for only 9 months in 2025 (flood closure), while policy requires a full-year basis. CORRECTION: Annualised West sales = £2.1m × 12/9 = £2.8m: £280 per sq ft of sales floor. The lowest full-year density is South at £240, so South gets the budget.
F4. [misreport] In 2024 West had the second-highest density (£2.9m / 10,000 = £290 per sq ft of sales floor). South was the weakest (£3.5m / 15,000 = £233). CORRECTION: West was not weak in 2024. Its 2025 'decline' is the closure, so there is no trend case for West; South was weakest in both years.

EXTENSIONS:
- Show the decision is robust: South is lowest on sales-floor density in both 2024 (£233) and annualised 2025 (£240), while on gross area South and East tie at £200 once West is annualised (£233), which shows why the KPI's definition matters.
- Check West's post-reopening run rate (monthly sales April-December vs the same months of 2024) to confirm that annualising is fair, i.e. that West did not reopen with depressed trade.
- Consider return on refurbishment rather than lowest density alone: e.g. South's large floor (15,000 sq ft) means each £10/sq ft uplift is worth £150,000 a year, more than in any other store.

FINAL VERSION:
# Refurbishment Budget: Store Productivity Review, FY2025

## Recommendation

**Allocate this year's refurbishment budget to South.** The policy KPI is annual sales per square foot of sales floor, measured on a full-year basis. On that measure South is the lowest of the five stores at **£240 per sq ft**. It was also the lowest in 2024.

## Approach

The policy sets two conditions:

1. **Denominator: sales floor area.** Gross internal area includes stockrooms, so it is not used.
2. **Full-year basis.** West was closed for flood repairs from January to March 2025, so its £2.1m covers only 9 trading months. To compare it fairly with stores that traded all 12 months, its sales are annualised on a straight-line basis: £2.1m × 12/9 = **£2.8m**. The repairs did not change West's layout, so its 10,000 sq ft sales floor still applies.

*Assumption:* The policy requires a full-year basis but does not say how to calculate it. This review uses straight-line annualisation. The policy owner may prefer another method, such as adding West's actual January–March 2024 sales. The sensitivity check below shows the recommendation is very unlikely to change under any reasonable method.

## Sales density, 2025 (policy basis)

| Store | Annual sales (full-year basis) | Sales floor (sq ft) | Sales per sq ft | Rank (1 = most productive) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Central | £4.2m | 12,000 | £350 | 1 |
| North | £2.4m | 8,000 | £300 | 2= |
| East | £1.8m | 6,000 | £300 | 2= |
| West | £2.8m (annualised from £2.1m over 9 months) | 10,000 | £280 | 4 |
| **South** | **£3.6m** | **15,000** | **£240** | **5 (least productive)** |

South is about 14% below the next-weakest store (West, £280) and about 31% below Central.

## Trend

| Store | 2024 sales per sq ft | 2025 sales per sq ft | Sales change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Central | £333 | £350 | +5.0% |
| North | £288 | £300 | +4.3% |
| East | £283 | £300 | +5.9% |
| West | £290 | £280 (annualised) | −3.4% (annualised) |
| South | £233 | £240 | +2.9% |

- **South** was the lowest-density store in both years, so its shortfall is persistent and not a one-year result. It is growing, but more slowly than Central, North and East, so its gap to those three stores widened:
  - Central: from £100 to £110 per sq ft.
  - North: from £54 to £60 per sq ft.
  - East: from £50 to £60 per sq ft.

  Its gap to West narrowed, from about £57 to £40, because West's annualised sales fell.
- **West** was the second most productive store in 2024. Most of its reported fall from £2.9m to £2.1m comes from the three-month closure. On an annualised basis its sales fell about 3%. That is worth monitoring, but it does not make West the weakest store.
- **Chain total:** Reported sales fell by £0.3m, from £14.4m to £14.1m. West accounts for this. Its sales fell £0.8m, made up of roughly £0.7m lost to the closure and about £0.1m of underlying decline. The four stores that traded all year grew from £11.5m to £12.0m (+4.3%). On an annualised basis the chain grew from £14.4m to £14.8m.

## Sensitivity check

**Annualisation method.** The decision depends on annualising West's sales. On unadjusted 9-month sales West would show £210 per sq ft and rank lowest, but the policy's full-year basis rules that reading out.

Straight-line annualisation ignores seasonality, and the bias probably favours West. West's nine trading months (April to December) include the Christmas peak. If January to March is a weaker-than-average quarter, the straight-line figure **overstates** West's true full year. The question is whether a realistic adjustment could push West below South.

- West falls below South only if its full-year sales are under £2.4m.
- That requires January–March sales under £0.3m. That would be about 12.5% of the year, against a pro-rata share of 25%, so Q1 would have to be roughly half its pro-rata share.
- *Judgement, not sourced:* a post-Christmas quarter is often weaker than average, but a shortfall that large would be unusual.

If West's 2024 monthly sales are available, they should be used to confirm this.

**Denominator.** The result depends on using sales floor area, as the policy specifies. On gross internal area, South and East would tie for lowest at £200 per sq ft, with West at £233 and North at £240. This is not a reason to change the method. It does show that the choice of denominator matters, so the KPI should be applied exactly as written.

## Considerations for South

- **Space use.** South has the largest sales floor in the chain (15,000 sq ft) but only mid-range sales. Part of the problem may be space: too much floor for its catchment, or floor that is poorly used. The refurbishment brief should therefore cover layout and space allocation as well as cosmetic works, including whether some floor could be released or reconfigured.
- **Local demand.** Run a short review of South's catchment and competition alongside the works. Refurbishment will not fix a weakness driven by local demand.
- **Timing.** The works will need full or partial closure, so schedule them outside peak trading periods.

## Measuring the result

Twelve months after completion, assess South on three measures:

1. **Sales per sq ft of sales floor**, compared with:
   - its pre-refurbishment level (£240 in 2025), and
   - the change across the rest of the chain over the same period, so that chain-wide trends are not mistaken for the effect of the works.
2. **Absolute sales** (£3.6m in 2025), compared with the same chain-wide change. If the refurbishment shrinks the sales floor, density will rise even if trading does not improve. Absolute sales show whether the store is actually selling more.
3. **Density on both floor areas.** If the sales floor changes, report post-refurbishment sales over both the original 15,000 sq ft and the new area. This separates the effect of better trading from the effect of a smaller denominator.

If South closes during the works, annualise its sales using the same method applied to West here.
